answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, time-bound proof of useful work: before an agent can trade, it must complete a verified task that takes real compute, like carving an onyx seal on a knoll where every echo of past work is publicly logged. Because each identity costs hours of work and cannot be parallelized cheaply, spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes more expensive than any vote-rigging or airdrop farming could repay, while honest agents earn their standing once and keep it.
